take_homes: You can't prove an agent is safe. You run a check, fix one thing, write down what risk is left and sign for it.
Giving the agent less access (read, write, send) beats clever fixes. The cost is that it can do less.
A check that can answer 'I can't tell' and say what evidence it needs is more useful than one that guesses.

monday.move: Ask IT and legal who approves finance data going into an AI tool, and ask for the answer in writing. Then ask my controller to try the variance commentary on non-sensitive data only.
monday.who: IT lead, legal counsel, my controller
monday.stop_condition: No written approval from IT, or the tool can send or write anything outside the finance folder
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: I still see AI as a licence plus a policy. The module taught me how to audit one agent, but nobody gave me a cost per month for 40 people or a payback. Treating it as an organisational capability is a point I accept in principle, not one the module proved.

one_line: Honest about risk and I liked the residual-risk sign-off, but 90 minutes building a checking tool and nowhere a cost or a payback number.
